title: Flutter widgets for Android and iOS, a page per platform, a new hero

entries.text: AI components, a new group: prompt input (grows, Enter sends, Stop while streaming), AI message (user bubble or assistant answer with copy, regenerate and thumbs, streaming caret), thinking (shimmer and steps), tool call (running, done, failed, input and output), sources (citation chips and source cards), prompt suggestions and token meter (context window use). All seven also have an HTML tag.

Flutter: 116 widgets for Android and iOS apps, one Dart file per widget, copy-paste like the React ones. Buttons, inputs, cards, dialogs, sheets, toasts, tabs, bottom nav, calendar, date and time pickers, chat, kanban, charts and more, with the same colours, radii, ten palettes and dark mode as the web components. The seven AI components (prompt input, AI message, thinking, tool call, sources, prompt suggestions, token meter) are Flutter widgets too.

CLI and MCP: befui add, init and list take --flutter (files go to lib/befui, relative imports, no dependencies). get_component accepts format: "flutter", get_flutter_rules returns the rules, and llms-flutter.txt lists every widget with an example.

Docs: every component has a React, an HTML and (where it exists) a Flutter tab, each on its own page with its own sidebar. Flutter pages show a working preview, a phone view, the example, the source and a properties table.

Docs: the home page hero is now a sheet of real, usable components that fills in once. Docs pages load on demand, which makes the first load about 22% smaller (gzipped), and the Flutter previews are WebP at a quarter of the size.
Settings layout: sections stack by the width of the panel, not the window, so the title and fields no longer get squeezed in a narrow preview.
HTML: the virtual list demo no longer ships 100,000 rows as a 5 MB file; it builds them in the page.

Docs site speed: the components and blocks pages no longer build every card and preview up front (the blocks page went from about 4,800 elements to about 900), the sidebar builds a group's links only when it is opened, and the scroll bar reads layout at most once per frame.

DESIGN.md (the design rules: colour, type, shape, motion, how to add a component) and COMPONENTS.md (every component and block, with whether it has an HTML tag and a Flutter widget). COMPONENTS.md is generated by npm run registry:build.

Docs site: component pages open faster (collapsed code blocks only highlight the lines you can see) and typing in the filter, the sidebar search and the playground no longer waits for the page to re-render. Sections of a page and each demo now rise in smoothly as they load.

title: Next.js fixes for four dashboards, safer remove, readable amber and orange

entries.text: Next.js: blocks that pass a function to a chart (finance, analytics, ecommerce and sales dashboards) now start with 'use client'. The check now flags any component that passes a function as a prop.

befui remove now looks at every source file under your folder (pages, libs, blocks), not just components, handles relative imports, and lets you remove two components that use each other in one command.
Themes: amber and orange use a deeper primary so links and active states are readable on white (4.5:1), and the test now checks primary text on the page background for every theme.
Chat app and calendar app no longer fail on plain http, where crypto.randomUUID does not exist.

title: Ten new page blocks and befui diff and remove

entries.text: Account and system pages: OTP verify (six-digit code with a resend countdown), onboarding wizard (four steps with validation), notifications page (All and Unread tabs) and a server error page (500 with a retry and an incident timeline).
Marketing and finance pages: a team page, a contact page (form with validation beside an FAQ) and a finance dashboard (balances, cash flow, spending by category, transactions).
App pages: a kanban board page (search, priority filter, task dialog, Alt and arrow keys to move cards), a chat app and a calendar app (add events in a dialog).

CLI: befui diff <name> shows how your copy of a component differs from the latest, and befui remove <name> deletes a component's files. Remove refuses while other files import it, unless you pass --force.

Blocks are now checked for accessibility in the test suite. That found and fixed unnamed progress bars in billing, campaign performance, leave approvals and project overview, and an empty table header in employee directory.

title: Next.js support, 108 more icons, brand logos and ten themes

entries.text: Next.js: components that use state, Radix or browser APIs now start with 'use client', so they work in the App Router with nothing to configure. Purely presentational ones (cards, badges, tables, icons) stay server components, and a build check stops a new component shipping without the directive.

Icons: 108 new ones, 389 in total. Arrows and corners, panel and layout controls, text-editor tools, file types, developer icons, drag handles and calendar variants, plus health, finance, chart, weather and transport sets.

Brand icons: 30 logos (Google, GitHub, Apple, X, Stripe, Visa and more) as single-colour SVGs that follow the text colour, with official colours in brandColors. Check each provider's rules before using one in an official sign-in button.

Themes: ten ready palettes (blue, indigo, violet, rose, red, emerald, teal, amber, orange, slate) for light and dark, all passing WCAG AA, on a new Themes page that recolours the docs live. befui init --theme rose writes one into your index.css.
Sign in and sign up now offer Continue with Google and GitHub buttons above an or divider.
Default dark theme: primary button text is now near-black instead of white, raising its contrast from 3.7 to 5.3 (WCAG AA). To keep the old look, set --primary-foreground back to #ffffff in .dark.

title: Tour keyboard and spotlight fixes, input group disabled styling

entries.text: Tour: arrow keys no longer fire with Alt, Ctrl, Cmd or Shift held, or while focus is in another widget on the page, and they swap in right-to-left pages. The spotlight no longer trails the target while the page scrolls, and never dims the whole page before it is positioned.
Input group: a disabled button inside an addon no longer dims the whole field; only a disabled input does.
Hover card: the docs now say what to keep out of it (links, buttons, anything essential), because the card cannot be reached with the keyboard.

title: Accessibility fixes: all 18 examples that failed the automated check now pass

entries.text: Field: the label is now tied to its control automatically, so clicking the label focuses the input and screen readers announce it. Before, you had to set htmlFor and id yourself.

Structure: the calendar is a real grid of rows and cells (same look, same keys), the file manager is a named listbox of options, the mention input is a text box that points at the active suggestion (a textarea cannot be a combobox), and accordion panels are named after their heading.

Names: progress bar and progress ring take an aria-label, the tag input keeps a name once tags replace its placeholder, the onboarding checklist names its bar, version log groups include the release number, the day agenda now-line has a role, and the typewriter and text reveal read their full text to screen readers.
Examples: sliders, the select, the tooltip icon buttons and the table progress bars now carry labels, so they show the right way to build them.

title: Seven missing basics: hover card, button and input groups, toggle group, navigation menu, menubar and tour

entries.text: Menus and previews: hover card for a preview that opens on hover or focus, menubar for File, Edit, View style bars, and a navigation menu with mega-menu panels.
Joined controls: button group and input group (text, icons or buttons attached to a field), and a toggle group that lets several buttons stay pressed for formatting toolbars.
Product tour: spotlight parts of the page one step at a time, with Back, Next, Skip, arrow keys, Escape and reduced-motion support.

title: 34 animated charts with how-to-read guides, 13 page blocks, 16 building parts and 90 more icons

entries.text: Chart guides: every chart page has a "New to this chart? Start here" panel that says what it shows, how to read it, when to use it and when to skip it. The same text is in llms-full.txt, so an AI can explain a chart to your users.
Everyday charts: pie, half donut, area (stacked or overlapping), stacked bar, histogram, lollipop, scatter or bubble, circle packing and word cloud. Each plays its entrance when scrolled into view.
Comparison charts: slope, dumbbell, bullet, butterfly, bump (rank over time), Pareto (the 80/20 view), waterfall, forecast with a confidence band and Marimekko.
Flow and hierarchy charts: Sankey, chord, treemap, sunburst and streamgraph. Ribbons draw in, tiles spring, rings sweep.
Circular charts: radial bar, radial line, rose and waffle. The radar (pentagon) chart now grows out from the center too.
Distribution and live charts: box plot, ridgeline, matrix heatmap, punch card, Venn, candlestick, and a live streaming chart that slides as new values arrive.

New blocks for common pages: analytics dashboard, ecommerce dashboard, project overview, user management, profile, billing, API keys, invoice, checkout, landing page, inbox, top-nav layout and a 404 page.
Page building parts: theme toggle, user menu, settings layout, description list, bar list, comparison table, invoice and landing sections (hero, feature grid, stats, FAQ, CTA banner, footer).
More building blocks: uptime bar for status pages, leaderboard with rank badges, rating breakdown for reviews, and a credit card preview that flips in 3D.
More everyday parts: week strip for picking a day, order tracker for delivery progress, diff viewer for before and after text, and a day agenda time grid with overlapping events.
About 90 new icons: arrows, finance, files, devices, status, layout, people and editor tools.
Chart entrances: sparkline, bar chart, donut and line chart now wipe, grow or sweep in when scrolled into view, and skip it for reduced motion.
AI docs: llms.txt now has a page-recipe section (which blocks and parts to combine for a dashboard, settings page, landing page and more) and a block index grouped by purpose.

Stat card: the delta line no longer wraps word by word and the sparkline no longer spills out of a narrow card; it drops below the number instead. Donut chart: the legend wraps under the ring in narrow cards.

title: Pivot and tree tables, week view, uploads with progress and auth blocks

entries.text: Pivot table: cross-tab of your rows with sum, count, average, min or max, totals and heat shading.
Tree table: rows with child rows, opened by click or arrow keys.
File uploader: several files at once with a progress bar each, cancel, retry and a concurrency limit.
Onboarding carousel: swipeable mobile intro with dots, Skip and a final Get started button.
Auth blocks: sign up with a password strength meter, and a four-step reset password flow.
Week view: the event calendar now switches between month and week, and the week lists every event.
Event calendar: a multi-day event now names itself once, on its first day and at the start of each week row, instead of on every day.
Changelog: every older release is rewritten with a bold label on each note, so it reads like the newer ones.
Version log: each release groups its notes under Added, Changed, Fixed and Removed, with a bold lead phrase on every note so a long release can be skimmed. Larger text and clearer spacing.
Event calendar: the "+n more" label no longer reads backwards in right-to-left pages.

title: Install flow, four new components, two blocks and locale support

entries.text: New components: phone input (country picker, E.164 output), signature pad, event calendar (month view, multi-day events) and virtual list for huge datasets.
New blocks: pricing page and settings page.
Install flow: every component page now shows the befui add command first, and has a Copy for AI button that copies the install line, an example and the full source.
RTL switch: every preview can be flipped right-to-left to check a component.

Locale support: calendar, date picker and range picker take a locale for month and weekday names and digits. Calendar flips its arrows and arrow-key movement in right-to-left pages, and the currency input and date picker use logical start and end spacing.

title: Animated changelog and a version log component

entries.text: Version log: an animated version history component. The rail draws and dots pop as releases scroll in, entries slide in one by one, releases fold open, with a version jump strip and a kind filter. The changelog page uses it.
Changelog page: a page on the docs site where you can click any component name to open it. Click any component name to open it.
Icons: 95 new ones (189 in total), covering devices and media, commerce, charts, text formatting, files, map and travel, status, playback and more. Find them on the Icons page.

title: Sixty new components, blocks and a smarter CLI

entries.text: Page furniture: changelog, testimonial card, comment thread, code block, status dot, table of contents.
Search and input helpers: search bar with live results, currency input, inline edit, filter bar, notification center, cookie consent.
Roles and access: permission matrix with per-column toggles and locked roles.
Tooltip: gets a title, keyboard shortcut, light style and arrow, plus InfoTip and TruncatedText.
Data table: row selection with bulk actions, a column menu, sticky header, toolbar slot, row action menus and clickable rows. Table gets a footer and caption.
Boards, feeds and menus: kanban, activity feed, context menu.
Loader: six animations, a bar and an overlay.
Date range picker: gets quick presets (Last 7 days, This month and more) and a day count.
Reports table block: search, filters, sorting, row actions and a details drawer.
Online shop: product card, coupon input, order summary.
Layout and lists: split pane, sortable list, navbar, bottom navigation, floating action button.
People and conversation: chat, mention input, profile card, terminal, error state, image viewer.
Charts and files: line chart, radar chart, audit log, file manager.
Mobile and uploads: swipe actions, pull to refresh, bottom sheet, date and time picker, image upload.
Avatar: gets presence dots, square shape, an extra-large size, hover names on groups and UserInfo.
Avatar upload: pick a photo and see it instantly.
Forms and settings: schema form (multi-step wizard), rich text editor, notification preferences, saved views.
Planning and flow: funnel chart, gantt chart, org chart, approval flow, onboarding checklist, tag manager.
Shortcuts dialog: press ? to open it. Also number formatting helpers.
Sales dashboard block: KPI cards, revenue line chart, funnel and top deals.
CLI: the update command adds missing animations to your index.css; befui add warns when one is missing. befui mcp runs an MCP server for AI tools.
Icons everywhere: every component now uses the built-in icon set. lucide-react is no longer installed by init.
Docs site: loads demos on demand (main bundle 1.4 MB down to 0.58 MB), and llms.txt is grouped by category with rules and a task map.
Time: time picker, analog clock, world clock, stopwatch, timer, countdown and relative time.
Data and display: heatmap and pricing card.
AI tooling: llms.txt and llms-full.txt, AGENTS.md rules written by init, a Use with AI page, and befui add all.

Inputs and forms: button, input, label and field, checkbox, switch, select, combobox, calendar, date picker, segmented, slider, radio group, rating, OTP input, tag input, number stepper, chip, color picker.
Display and motion: accordion, spotlight card, border beam, marquee, carousel, compare, tilt card, shimmer text, typewriter, confetti, dock, collapsible, tree view.
Data and layout: data table, gauge, progress ring, number ticker, stat card, charts, sidebar, app shell.
Feedback and overlays: banner, alert, toast, skeleton, dialog and sheet, alert dialog, dropdown menu, popover, tooltip, command palette.
Foundations: a built-in icon set, Storybook, the befui CLI (init, add, list), and HRMS and marketing blocks.
